---
title: "Releasing"
description: >-
  How a release is made: the version, update.json, why commit and release belong together, and how the documentation is versioned.
---

1. Bump `version` in `addon/manifest.json`, and `softwareVersion` in both
   `doc/en/index.qmd` and `doc/de/index.qmd`
2. `python3 script/gen_versions.py`, then `./build.sh`
3. Commit the regenerated `update.json` and `versions.json` with them —
   `test/release.test.mjs` holds all of these to the manifest
4. Create the release with the built `.xpi` attached

`update.json` must be committed to `main`, because that is the URL installed
copies poll.

::: {.callout-important title="Commit and release belong together"}
`update.json` carries the version, the download URL and the checksum. Pushing it
for a version that has no release yet means every installed copy sees an update
and runs into nothing when it tries to fetch it.

Equally, a local build of an already-released state must not be committed: its
checksum differs as soon as anything in the code has changed. `test/release.test.mjs`
catches that, and the failure means *bump the version*, not *update the hash*.
:::

## What is kept, between builds

A kept preview is keyed on the build that made it — the version, and the stamp
`build.sh` writes into the package. The version alone would tell one release
from another, which is all a user needs; it would not tell one build of 1.2.0
from the next, which is what anyone working on a version needs. Without the
stamp a preview made by the first build is handed back by the second, and the
change appears not to have arrived.

Entries made by any other build are removed at startup, along with the layout
of earlier versions, which nothing reads any more and nothing else would ever
clear.

## Compatibility

The update entry deliberately carries **no `strict_max_version`**. Zotero then
treats the release as compatible with any version and can raise the ceiling on
an already-installed copy — which is how compatibility with a future Zotero can
be granted without shipping a new build.

The `strict_max_version` in `manifest.json` still decides which Zotero will load
the plugin at all.

## Documentation

The published documentation lives under a directory per release, with `latest`
a second copy of the newest one, so a link that was published keeps pointing at
what it pointed at. `versions.json` is the list the version switcher reads, and
`script/gen_versions.py` keeps it in step with the version the manifest
reports.

Adding a version is a change to a committed file, deliberately: a release that
quietly appeared in the switcher and nowhere else would be hard to account for
later.
